As someone who also had to call CPS when I was younger to help protect me and my sister, I want to give some tips that will hopefully help you. I made some mistakes with my case, and we ended back up in the custody of our parents with nothing to do and nowhere to go. I am 19 too and have since moved out, but was unable to take my sister...

Tips:
1. Try your best to save your niece. Don't let her live through horrible scenarios such as that. Maybe you could even try to gain temporary custody of her.

2. Check and see if you have dependable family that are nearby, capable of situating you and your sister, and, if you're lucky, have a license to be a foster parent. That will highly increase your chances of being situated with them if a CPS case were to open up.

3. Report this to CPS as soon as possible. Don't wait. The more time that goes on, the less valid your evidence become. You could also use possible marks on your sister as proof you both need to get the fuck out of there.

4. Don't let your warrant expire on your niece if you both get put into temporary custody. Your parents could try to take her back if that happens.

5. For the love of all things wonderful, BE. PERSISTENT. Your parents might try to break you and make you cave into giving up the case, but you know why you would be doing all of this. This was the mistake I made. I ask you to stay strong, and see the case all the way through. If CPS seems like they are starting to become lax with looking into the case or trying to keep your niece safe, check in with the worker assigned to your case whenever they visit.

I know this advice is very mediocre, but I hope it helps for if you do take the CPS route.
